title: SWR
blurb: Forward and reflected power on the feed line, and what 1:1 means.

lines.caption: Your transmitter sends power along the feed line to the antenna. Call it forward power.
When the antenna is well matched to the feed line, it takes that power and radiates it.
When the match is poor, some power is reflected back down the line toward your radio.
SWR, standing wave ratio, is a measure of how well a load is matched to a transmission line.
A reading of 1:1 is a perfect match. No power comes back.
A reading like 4:1 means an impedance mismatch.
High SWR matters. Most solid-state transmitters cut their output power as SWR rises, to protect the output transistors.
You can check it with an SWR meter or a directional wattmeter.
